author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The University of Rhode Island will hold its second annual Technology Showcase on September 22, bringing university researchers, startup founders, investors and industry representatives together in Kingston.

The event is scheduled for 4 to 7 p.m. at Toray Commons in the Fascitelli Center for Advanced Engineering. It is part of Rhode Island Startup Week and is designed to move research toward licensing, partnerships and new ventures.

URI said featured work will include smart-wound monitoring and PFAS detection. The university also pointed to recent commercialization activity: spinout Juice Robotics has licensed four URI technologies, Trace Sensing closed a seed round of more than $2 million and FastFlowLM joined an AMD program.

Those examples do not guarantee that every project at the showcase will attract funding or reach the market. They illustrate the event’s purpose: giving potential backers and partners an early look at applied research. Registration and the final program are available through URI, and schedule details may change before September 22.
dek: The September 22 event will put university inventions and startups in front of investors and industry partners during Rhode Island Startup Week.
headline: URI technology showcase will connect research with investors
